cultural.vision_reason: The object is a carved, polychrome wooden dance-wand with a painted human face, fretwork headdress, feather plume, and fibre beard, used in dance/ritual performance — a type of carved ritual object associated with Tolai and neighbouring New Britain peoples.

physical.title: dance-wand; bead
physical.summary: Flat wood polychrome dance-wand, carved and painted on both sides, in form of human face with tall fretwork headdress terminating in plume of white, yellowish and black feathers. Below face sub-triangular grip, upper part of which is painted brown. Both faces are painted blue, yellow, green, red and white; tooth-edged eyes of pearl-shell, rubber (?) and white beads. One eye missing from one face, which has in addition stick nose-pin. Fibre beards on both faces, greyish black "hair" of feathers. Fretwork headdress painted white, blue and red with circular, toothed-edge ornament of pearl-shell, rubber (?), paper and glass bead at the base on both sides, and yellow feather decoration on each side below the plume.
